question: A 45-year-old woman, gravida 3, para 2, at 18 weeks' gestation comes to the physician for a prenatal visit. Ultrasonography at a previous visit when she was at 12 weeks' gestation showed a hypoplastic nasal bone. Pelvic examination shows a uterus consistent in size with an 18-week gestation. Maternal serum studies show low α-fetoprotein and free estriol concentrations, and increased inhibin A and β-hCG concentrations. Physical examination of the infant after delivery is most likely to show which of the following findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hypoplastic nasal bone on ultrasound at 12 weeks" -> "Low α-fetoprotein and free estriol concentrations" -> "Increased inhibin A and β-hCG concentrations" -> "Increased risk of Down syndrome" -> "Physical examination of the infant after delivery may show ambiguous external genitalia" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Low α-fetoprotein and free estriol concentrations" -> "Increased inhibin A and β-hCG concentrations" -> "Increased risk of placental abnormalities" -> "Physical examination of the infant after delivery may show meningomyelocele" -> 70%
analysis: The combination of hypoplastic nasal bone on ultrasound, low α-fetoprotein and free estriol concentrations, and increased inhibin A and β-hCG concentrations are suggestive of a chromosomal abnormality, specifically trisomy 21 (Down syndrome). Infants with Down syndrome commonly present with certain physical features, one of which is a single transverse palmar crease.
